The Lord of the Rings. J.R.R. Tolkien's monumental epic fantasy about the quest to destroy an ancient ring of power forged by a dark sorcerer. Set in the fictional world of Middle-earth, it follows a small hobbit named Frodo Baggins as he journeys from his pastoral homeland toward Mount Doom to unmake the ring and defeat his enemy. The trilogy fundamentally shaped modern fantasy literature and established the template for epic quest narratives.

Composed of three volumes—The Fellowship of the Ring, The Two Towers, and The Return of the King—originally written as a single work but split for publication. The story centers on hobbits, small peaceful beings from the Shire, as heroes, a radical departure from sword-swinging warrior protagonists.

The Ring itself is a tool of corruption; even the protagonist's uncle Bilbo, who found it decades earlier, becomes obsessed and possessive. The work features Gandalf the Grey, a wizard whose apparent death and return mirrors the hero's resurrection across mythic narratives.

The Fellowship includes members from different races—hobbits, elf, dwarf, human, wizard—creating a multicultural heroic team. Informed by Tolkien's academic expertise in medieval literature, Norse mythology, and Old English, the epic drew parallels to World War II despite predating it.

The narrative spans vast territories and multiple years; Frodo and his companions face increasingly dire challenges including encounters with Balrogs, ancient demons, and supernatural evil. Tolkien created an entirely constructed world with invented languages, genealogies, and historical depth spanning thousands of years—unprecedented worldbuilding for fiction.

The ending is bittersweet: Frodo succeeds in his quest, but bears psychological scars; he must depart Middle-earth entirely, leaving his homeland forever. The trilogy spawned countless imitators and became the template for modern fantasy; it influenced decades of literature, games, and films, inspiring an Academy Award-winning film trilogy.

J.R.R. Tolkien is the philologist and medievalist whose life work culminated in this invented world. Fantasy is the foundational modern fantasy epic that codified the genre's conventions. Mythology means Tolkien modeled his work after Norse and Anglo-Saxon myths; the trilogy functions as a modern mythology. The epic quest is the hero's journey structure, drawn from classical epics like The Odyssey. Power and corruption is the ring's seductive influence on all who possess it, regardless of moral intent. Coming of age describes how Frodo and his hobbit companions grow from innocence to wisdom through trials.
